newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds firmed on Tuesday, notably at the longer end, with supportive German, then U.S. data, and some squeezing of domestic shorts.
"All the data looks pretty positive. Some went short into the U.S. numbers and then had to cover," one trader said.
This morning's German M3 money supply growth for July, at an annualised 5.7 percent, was below expectations.
Housing starts in the United States were unchanged in July at an annualised 1.447 million, also below most estimates.
Dutch bonds all firmed, with the curve again flattening.
Traders said institutions were again more interested in buying longer dated paper.
One player said there had been a sizeable buyer of February 2007s, but otherwise outright buyers, as opposed to short coverers and portfolio adjusters, were not plentiful.
Traders said the next focus of attention would be the outcome of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting, due after the close of trading today. Few expected U.S. interest rate changes to result.
"The equity markets are also quite nervous still. So we're expecting little from the U.S. this evening," one trader said.
